subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence contract for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while relying on heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config/API shape rather than fixing a broken existing contract.

options.title: Design cron every phase/stagger
options.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve current anchored fixed-interval semantics and close or mark this feature not planned for cron `every`.

options.title: Add broader prime mode
options.body: Accept a larger product surface covering prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron.

recommendation.title: Design cron every phase/stagger
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current cron stagger surface and are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether `every` should gain a related public contract.
